Before this last patch: not really. They were mostly just sorting filenames and using the scheduled run time implicitly.

Now, yes. I added explicit current-date awareness:

- [release-summary-slack-v2.yml](/Users/goose-guest/Documents/agent-experiments/cli/.github/workflows/release-summary-slack-v2.yml:42) sets `CURRENT_DATE` in `America/New_York`, filters dispatch files to only dates `<= CURRENT_DATE`, then picks the latest.

- Last 3 style references are also filtered to today-or-earlier, so future-dated drafts won’t sneak in.
- [Release Summary](/Users/goose-guest/Documents/agent-experiments/cli/.github/workflows/release-summary-slack-v2.yml:231) now calls `entire dispatch --until now` explicitly.
- [Dispatch Notes](/Users/goose-guest/Documents/agent-experiments/cli/.github/workflows/release-notes-slack.yml:663) uses that shared current date for the Slack output date too.

I verified the filter locally: with current date `2026-05-29`, it picks `2026-05-26-entire-dispatch-0x000f.mdx`; with current date `2026-05-20`, it correctly falls back to `2026-05-18-entire-dispatch-0x000e.mdx`. YAML parse and `git diff --check` pass.
do you think it's valuable to know current date or is that silly

Not silly. I’d keep it.

The `.md` vs `.mdx` mismatch was the real bug, but current date awareness is a useful guardrail. It prevents the workflow from accidentally treating a future-dated dispatch draft as “latest,” and it gives the model an explicit window: from the last published dispatch through today.

The key is not to overuse it. Current date should be a boundary, not the source of truth. Source of truth is still: “latest dispatch post in `entire.io` dated on or before today.” That’s the right shape.
okay im wondering if the output can go into these markdown files for me..rather than just outputting in slack text..you get me..like if it goes into a text snippet file for markdown

I get you: instead of flooding Slack with long rendered text, make the workflow produce a real `.md` file and upload it as a Markdown/snippet-style file, with only a short Slack note around it. I’m checking Slack’s current file-upload API shape before editing, because their older upload endpoint changed recently.

This is a good fit for Slack file upload: the workflow can keep generating `.md` files, then share the file in Slack with a short comment instead of splitting the whole thing into chat messages. Slack’s current docs say to use `files.getUploadURLExternal` followed by `files.completeUploadExternal`, so I’m swapping the text-posting sections over to that flow.

Yes, exactly: if `Release Summary to Slack V2` was already running when the PR merged, it did **not** pick up the merged changes mid-run.

GitHub Actions runs are tied to the commit/ref that triggered them. GitHub’s docs say reruns use the same `GITHUB_SHA` and `GITHUB_REF` as the original run, so a normal “Re-run failed jobs” can still use the old version of the workflow. Source: [GitHub Docs on re-running workflows](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/managing-workflow-runs-and-deployments/managing-workflow-runs/re-running-workflows-and-jobs?tool=cli).

So for your case:

- If the `Release Summary` run started before PR #30 merged, that failure probably does **not** prove #30 failed.
- Don’t click “Re-run failed jobs” on that old run if you want the new workflow code.
- Start a **new** workflow run from the Actions tab using `workflow_dispatch` on `main`.
- For scheduled runs, the next schedule should use the merged workflow on `main`.

I started a more conservative patch after seeing the failure, but given this timing, I’d pause that and first run a fresh workflow from `main`. That will tell us whether #30 actually fixed it.
